body.statement: For every finite input \(\mathfrak u\) accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\), every \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), and every \(D\in\mathfrak D\), the law \(p\) is Markov to \(D\). Hence the intersection of the represented DAG Markov models with the exact oracle model is exactly \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), and no graph-local Markov generator strengthens \(J_{\mathcal I}\) on this domain.
body.justification: This reduction prevents the minimum-edge promise from being mistaken for extra observed-law equations.
body.gap: Raskutti and Uhler define sparsest I-maps, but do not isolate the common-law model needed for cross-graph effects.
body.consumer: The algebraic certificate generator can omit redundant graph-local minors and report a smaller verified ideal.
body.proof_tex:
Fix an accepted input \(\mathfrak u\), a table \(p\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\), and a graph \(D\in\mathfrak D\).  Write \(\operatorname{CI}(D)\) for the elementary conditional-independence statements implied by d-separation in \(D\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}sparsest\text{-}dag\text{-}family}\), retention of \(D\) means precisely that
\[
 \operatorname{CI}(D)\subseteq\{c:\mathcal I(c)=1\}. \tag{1}
\]
For every statement \(c\) in the set on the right, \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}oracle\text{-}model}\) and the oracle-one condition say that every determinantal minor encoding \(c\) vanishes at \(p\).  Thus every member of \(\operatorname{CI}(D)\) holds under \(p\).  This is the global Markov property of \(p\) with respect to \(D\).  Since \(D\) was arbitrary,
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}
 \subseteq\bigcap_{D\in\mathfrak D}\mathcal M(D), \tag{2}
\]
where \(\mathcal M(D)\) is the set of probability laws globally Markov to \(D\).  Intersecting both sides of (2) with \(\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}\cap
 \bigcap_{D\in\mathfrak D}\mathcal M(D)
 =\mathcal M_{\mathcal I}^{\circ}. \tag{3}
\]

Finally, a graph-local Markov determinantal generator for \(D\) encodes a statement in \(\operatorname{CI}(D)\).  By (1), that statement has oracle bit one, and by the definition of \(\mathcal C_1(\mathcal I)\), the same minor is already a generator of
\[
 J_{\mathcal I}
 =\left\langle\mathcal C_1(\mathcal I),
       \sum_{z\in\Omega}p_z-1\right\rangle. \tag{4}
\]
Consequently adjoining graph-local Markov minors changes neither this ideal nor its zero set on the declared exact-oracle domain.  Equations (2)--(4) prove all assertions.
